cases.excerpt: We conducted a nested case-control study, 1,263 prostate cancer cases and 2,346 controls, sampled from participants in the Multiethnic Cohort Study with pre-diagnostic urine samples assayed for 6-sulfatoxymelatonin, the primary melatonin metabolite. Conditional logistic regression was used to examine the association between melatonin levels and the development of prostate cancer outcomes (all incident cases, advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive), overall and by race/ethnicity.

effect_size.excerpt: Neither unadjusted nor adjusted models showed an association between urinary melatonin and overall prostate cancer (OR continuous : 1.01, 0.93-1.09; OR Q4vsQ1 : 1.06, 0.85-1.32).

extraction_supporting_text.cases: We conducted a nested case-control study, 1,263 prostate cancer cases and 2,346 controls, sampled from participants in the Multiethnic Cohort Study with pre-diagnostic urine samples assayed for 6-sulfatoxymelatonin, the primary melatonin metabolite. Conditional logistic regression was used to examine the association between melatonin levels and the development of prostate cancer outcomes (all incident cases, advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive), overall and by race/ethnicity.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Neither unadjusted nor adjusted models showed an association between urinary melatonin and overall prostate cancer (OR continuous : 1.01, 0.93-1.09; OR Q4vsQ1 : 1.06, 0.85-1.32).

evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test was not performed because fewer than 10 studies were available. With a small number of studies, the test generally has insufficient power to reliably detect funnel plot asymmetry.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.45–1.23), indicating no statistically significant association between melatonin and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 73.01%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
